content.comment_body: I'm using a [product_name] to measure machine RPM, with a maximum value of 6500. A 12V NPN sensor and a pull-up resistor are connected. I believe the 5kHz specification of the [product_name] should be sufficient, but when the motor reaches full speed, it doesn't register correctly.

Offtopic: Is the background of the diagram set to green? Back to topic: Fast counter inputs can only be counted accurately if directly connected to the counter input or threshold switch (frequency), without additional logic in between. [company_name] guarantees reliable operation up to 5 kHz.

Offtopic: You can adjust this option in Tools/Options. I'm colorblind so this helps distinguish the lines better. On topic: I wasn't aware of the direct connection requirement. I ran a quick test, it worked—thanks!
I'm aware of that, but I find your configuration hard to read when reviewing a program. It's visually straining for me...

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced challenges measuring machine RPM at high speed using a [product_name] with high-speed counter inputs. Initially, the counter failed to record correctly when the machine was running at maximum speed. Discussion revealed that accurate readings for fast pulses require a direct connection to the counter input, matching the product’s 5kHz rating. After applying this approach, testing confirmed successful operation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] to consistently and accurately record rapid input signals for machine RPM, especially at maximum operational speeds, fulfilling the advertised capability of up to 5kHz.
pain_keywords: lack of clarity on direct input requirement
